claim: DeepSeek-V3 states that the communication overhead introduced by cross-node expert parallelism produces an inefficient computation-to-communication ratio of approximately 1:1 — i.e. on an NVLink+IB cluster, EP all-to-all cost roughly as much wall time as the compute it fed.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP's all-to-all is a first-order cost that rules EP out on a much slower fabric
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 671B MoE training on 2048 H800 GPUs, intra-node NVLink + inter-node InfiniBand, EP32
quoted_support: For DeepSeek-V3, the communication overhead introduced by cross-node expert parallelism results in an inefficient computation-to-communication ratio of approximately 1:1.

claim: DualPipe hides both all-to-all and pipeline communication behind compute by splitting each chunk into attention, all-to-all dispatch, MLP and all-to-all combine and rearranging forward/backward chunks, reaching 'near-zero all-to-all communication overhead' as long as the compute-to-communication ratio is held constant.
stance_target: the claim that EP cost can only be removed by overlap, not by a cheaper collective
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 training; DualPipe bidirectional pipeline scheduling with 8 PP ranks and 20 micro-batches
quoted_support: In this overlapping strategy, we can ensure that both all-to-all and PP communication can be fully hidden during execution. ... This overlap also ensures that, as the model further scales up, as long as we maintain a constant computation-to-communication ratio, we can still employ fine-grained experts across nodes while achieving a near-zero all-to-all communication overhead.

claim: The overlap is engineered around a two-tier fabric: intra-node NVLink at 160 GB/s versus inter-node IB at 50 GB/s (3.2x), with each token dispatched to at most 4 nodes, averaging 3.2 experts per node, and only 20 SMs dedicated to saturating both links.
stance_target: the claim that EP's standard mitigations presuppose a fast intra-node tier and a separate scale-out network, neither of which a flat Gen2 x4 box has
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 H800 cluster: NVLink intra-node, IB inter-node; custom cross-node all-to-all kernels
quoted_support: NVLink offers a bandwidth of 160 GB/s, roughly 3.2 times that of IB (50 GB/s). To effectively leverage the different bandwidths of IB and NVLink, we limit each token to be dispatched to at most 4 nodes, thereby reducing IB traffic. ... only 20 SMs are sufficient to fully utilize the bandwidths of IB and NVLink.
numbers: up to 13 experts at same cost

claim: DeepSeek-V3 was trained without tensor parallelism at all — the memory optimizations 'enabl[ed] us to train DeepSeek-V3 without using costly Tensor Parallelism (TP)' — so the lab with the strongest incentive to use TP chose EP32 + DP instead.
stance_target: the repo's claim that tensor parallelism is ruled out for training on this box
quoted_support: Finally, we meticulously optimize the memory footprint during training, thereby enabling us to train DeepSeek-V3 without using costly Tensor Parallelism (TP).

claim: The training topology is EP32 with DP, and inference uses TP4 + SP + DP8 + EP32 for prefill and EP320 for decode — TP is confined to small degrees and to the inference side.
stance_target: what degree of TP a production MoE stack tolerates even on a fast fabric
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 deployment on H800 cluster; prefill minimum unit 4 nodes / 32 GPUs
quoted_support: The attention part employs 4-way Tensor Parallelism (TP4) with Sequence Parallelism (SP), combined with 8-way Data Parallelism (DP8). Its small TP size of 4 limits the overhead of TP communication. For the MoE part, we use 32-way Expert Parallelism (EP32).

claim: Training cost datapoint: 14.8T tokens on 2048 H800 GPUs costs 2.664M GPU hours for pretraining (~180K H800 GPU-hours per trillion tokens), 2.788M GPU hours and ~$5.576M in total — a reference for what a well-provisioned MoE pretraining run costs.
stance_target: the scale gap between a 2048-GPU H800 cluster and a 5-GPU CMP 170HX box
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 pretraining + context extension + post-training; $2/H800 GPU-hour assumption
quoted_support: During the pre-training stage, training DeepSeek-V3 on each trillion tokens requires only 180K H800 GPU hours, i.e. 3.7 days on our cluster with 2048 H800 GPUs. ... DeepSeek-V3 costs only 2.788M GPU hours for its full training.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 is a 671B-total / 37B-active MoE with MLA attention and DeepSeekMoE (8 routed experts plus 1 shared expert per layer), i.e. a ~5.5% activation ratio at 671B scale.
stance_target: what total-to-active ratio a 1B-scale MoE experiment should imitate
quoted_support: We present DeepSeek-V3, a strong Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 671B total parameters with 37B activated for each token.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 uses auxiliary-loss-free load balancing (a per-expert bias term adjusted during training) instead of an auxiliary balancing loss, which avoids the quality trade-off that balancing losses impose — the same design family as Routing-Free MoE's threshold/bias approach.
stance_target: the claim that MoE load balancing can be handled without a quality penalty, which matters for small-scale MoE experiments
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 pretraining; DeepSeekMoE with auxiliary-loss-free balancing
quoted_support: Firstly, DeepSeek-V3 pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy to mitigate the performance degradation induced by load balancing.

claim: The report's EP optimizations are co-designed with a specific cluster topology (fully-interconnected IB across nodes plus NVLink within nodes); a 5-GPU box with no NVLink, no P2P and no scale-out network has neither tier, so neither the hierarchical dispatch nor the SM-budget trick transfers.
stance_target: whether DeepSeek's EP mitigations can be ported to the CMP 170HX box
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3 H800 cluster network; comparison to a flat PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric
quoted_support: The implementation of the kernels is co-designed with the MoE gating algorithm and the network topology of our cluster. To be specific, in our cluster, cross-node GPUs are fully interconnected with IB, and intra-node communications are handled via NVLink.
